title: In search of lost domain generalization
relevance: The canonical corrective to the whole domain-generalization literature: with careful implementation and honest model selection, plain empirical risk minimization matches or beats every DG algorithm tested across seven datasets. Their sharper claim is the one that binds us - a DG algorithm WITHOUT a stated model-selection strategy should be regarded as INCOMPLETE, because selecting on target-domain data silently leaks the thing you claim to generalize to. That is precisely our unexamined weak point: we select on validation built from projected 2020 labels, so our model selection is neither in-domain nor honestly out-of-domain. Read alongside Brigato 2021 (ID 137) - two independent canonical results saying a properly tuned and properly selected baseline is the thing every fancier proposal must beat.

authors: Khoee, A.G., Yu, Y. & Feldt, R.
title: Domain generalization through meta-learning: a survey
relevance: Covers the one DG family this loop had never touched, and the survey plus its surrounding literature effectively rules it out for us: episodic meta-learning is built for FAST ADAPTATION given a few target examples, while domain generalization assumes ZERO target examples, and with few source domains the task-generation capacity collapses into overfitting to training tasks. We have exactly one labelled domain, which is the worst case for it. Value here is negative-space value - it lets us close a family with a reason rather than leaving it as an unexplored maybe.
